newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK CIVIL SERVANTS AHEAD OF 97 INFLATION CURVE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK CIVIL SERVANTS AHEAD OF 97 INFLATION CURVE.

text.p: The Greek government bowed to pressure from the civil servants' union (ADEDY) and revised the unified pay scale for civil servants to include pay rises higher than expected inflation, finance ministry figures showed.

Deputy Finance Minister Nickos Christodoulakis was quoted as saying in the Greek press that civil servants would be better off under the new unified pay scale instead of the 2.5 percent inflation catch up and two extra pay rises totaling 4.5 percent.
ADEDY leaders were quoted as saying that they were not happy with the new pay scale despite acknowledging that improvements had been made.

Under the new unified pay scale, various bonuses for different classes of civil servants will be grouped together. Yet a number of bonuses such as family and children allowances will remain and will be raised significantly.
It was unclear what kind of pay rises civil servants from different ministries would get but they should surpass the 7.0 percent figure.
In the past, civil servants were getting a small base salary that was taxable and a myriad of bonuses that were exempt from taxation.
Civil servants got hefty salary increases of 13 to 19 percent in 1996 via productivity bonuses according to market analysts.

The Greek government expects CPI-based inflation to be at 4.5 percent year-on-year at end-97. The national economy ministry forecasts that the private consumption deflator will drop to 6.5 percent on average in 1997 from an estimated 8.5 percent in 1996.

Headline inflation fell to 7.5 percent year-on-year in December from 8.1 percent in December 1995 but core inflation stood at 8.2 percent year-on-year in December from 9.1 percent in December 1995. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
